## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b741f8255d645c9ab72053afb28cd4cd4d3c4a56`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md + scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs

Inputs read: card #33751 body and both comments (claim 6892768967, dev report 6893055822), pilot card #33059 and its comments, PR #33777 body and file list (4 files, +88 -2), the net diff against merge base `12a0f09fca49` (head is 2 ahead, 7 behind main), and the check-runs on the head. Check-runs on the head, all completed: 26 success, 23 skipped, 0 failed, none running; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (the line ratchet among its gates), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and both `Test Core` shards are success.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set and public surface: no change. The diff is three `.claude/**` rule-text files and one PM gate script; no package, no schema, no export. `Clause-②: no` is right, `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- Governed tier: Tier S is right. All three governed paths are `.claude/**`, which AGENTS.md Prime Directive 14 and SKILL.md 路径分叉 both place in Tier S; `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` is not on the register. The card's Reader section says "Tier H, needs os-zhuang or hotlong approval": that sentence is stale against the register and is not followed. Landing is by the owning seat through the queue on a current-head at-tier PASS with no should-fix open.
- Tier of authoring: `dispatch-gates --tier` reads MANDATORY from the SKILL.md path. Drafting at the default tier is allowed by execution-duties.md (references-only surface, or a one-line mechanical edit on a governed file, with the at-tier review as the compensating control). This record is that at-tier read. Right.
- Ceiling raise SKILL.md 319 to 320: right in amount (measured delta +1, the row moves by exactly 1, no other row moves). On authority: the ratchet header asks for the id of the ruling that orders text into the file. The ruling here has no comment of its own; the maintainer's words are quoted verbatim in the card body under filing gate ③, and the row cites the card body plus the claim comment id. That is the same convention as the already-landed seat-lifecycle.md row for the previous raise, so it is accepted. Note for the seat record: the card ordered the lane line in `lanes/*.md`, not in SKILL.md; the row comment says so honestly, and see ④ for why the index row is the better place.
- Ceiling raise seat-lifecycle.md 99 to 100: right. The card names this file and this line; delta +1, row moves by 1.
- New CEILINGS row area-lease.md 60 and MAX_TABLE_ROW_BYTES row 0: right. The file is 60 lines at the head, carries no table row, its longest line is 120 bytes, and a new file is an added row. The card orders the new reference.
- Lane line as one SKILL.md index row: right. SKILL.md 优先级 says the phase files and their readers are found in 阶段细则索引, and every lane seat reads SKILL.md on every fire; a line in each lane charter would be read by one lane each and would raise up to fifteen ceilings. The row is 175 bytes, under the 341-byte pin.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` matches the diff: nothing published changes. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.

Clause-②: no — confirmed from the committed tree (no `packages/**` path, no published schema, no narrowing arm).

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, tier: answered in ① (allowed, compensated by this record).
- Deviation, signed HTML trailer on the PR body: required by seat-post-protocol.md (PR body last line), so it is correct for a relay-written PR.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: relay-written, no off-relay author note owed.
- Omission 1, "a clean main merge with the same patch-id keeps the PASS": sound. contract-review.md owns head moves and carries a record only across a pure regeneration or a prose-only move; landing-operations.md sends a main merge to that same line; the queue guard reads a current-head record. Writing the card's sentence would contradict the owner and the guard. The new file points at contract-review.md. If the carry is wanted it needs its own card on contract-review.md.
- Omission 2, "a seat ruling that changes observable behaviour or interprets an ADR gets one independent review first": the omission is sound, the stated reason is overstated. The two rules are compatible in the letter: an independent review before a seat acts is an added control, and nothing in the no-proxy-ruling red line forbids one. But the card's sentence presupposes that a seat may rule on observable behaviour, and SKILL.md does not allow that at all (red line: seats analyse and recommend; 升级与决策: touching product behaviour or contract shape is a fork for a human). Written into the skill it would read as "reviewed, therefore the seat may decide", which is the proxy channel the red line closes. What remains inside seat discretion (precedent-named keys under the veto window, the non-escalation classes) already has its second read in execution-duties.md (a seat that thinks a ruling should move sends it to a review thread before dispatch). So nothing the card needs is lost. The seat names this in its ACCEPT as an accepted deviation from card §3, since §3 orders "§2.4 rules" whole.
- Omission 3, `claude/area-*` branch names: sound. AGENTS.md names branches `claude/issue-N-SLUG`, its force-push criterion reads that prefix, and AGENTS.md outranks `.claude/**`. The area id travels on the `lease:` label and the lease table.
- Out-of-scope findings in the dev report all name the skills seat as carrier; the seat answers each in its ACCEPT. One of them is a real follow-up, see nit N3.
- Security: none found. Nothing in the diff puts a security finding on GitHub; the new file sends security to security-findings.md.

### ④ Design judgment

Read against card §3, the pilot record on #33059, and the cited references in the head tree and on current main (queue.md, review.md, contract-review.md, seat-lifecycle.md, execution-duties.md, project-forms.md, SKILL.md are identical on main to the head tree apart from this PR's lines, except queue.md, which gained the relay dequeue door on main and keeps the line cited in S1).

What holds:
- Coverage of card §3 is complete apart from the three declared omissions: dynamic partitioning (whether, how many, boundaries, at seating and at every hand-over or shift, merge and split, lease table on the seat post, review seats scaling), startup with both authorising lines verbatim, W0, the in-area rules, the per-round re-check of PASS'd governed PRs, mailbox on every seating, cross-account hand-over and ownership split on the seat post, lessons 5, 6 and 7.
- The authorising line cannot be satisfied by a relay: "只认本线程维护者原话,转述与点选不算", and the next line says it does not change the Prime Directive 14 landing tier. Good.
- No area can land a governed PR or a PR over 3,000 lines: both go to the seat, Tier S included, which matches "the owning seat lands it". The Tier H hand-off is a pointer to SKILL.md 路径分叉 ①–④, not the card's own four pieces. That matters: the card's list has `pr_ready` before approval, which the red line forbids, and the pointer avoids restating it.
- Pointers resolve: the atomic claim pair, the five fold gates and the per-round four-piece line exist in execution-duties.md; the three jump reasons exist in landing-operations.md; the mailbox key `Request: contract-review` is the spelling in project-forms.md; the hand-over checklist exists in seat-post-protocol.md; self-triage lives in triage-duties.md.
- The moving-seat line in seat-lifecycle.md agrees with project-forms.md (a mailbox is keyed by seat, a new one on any account change; an account takes an empty seat when its own is taken) and with card §2.5.
- Nothing server-specific remains outside the worked example, apart from nit N1.
- scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs agrees with the contract line by line: three ceiling values equal the landed counts, each raised row quotes the ruling words and the measured delta, headroom 0, no cross-file move declared and none needed.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix) — queue-duty fallback contradicts its owner.** area-lease.md line 14: "队列值守归在座 `queue#N`;无则一复核席兼 `lanes/queue.md`". lanes/queue.md says "本席未开时,分诊在每小时巡查里临时兼本章程", and lanes/review.md says a review seat "⛔ 不 merge、不 ready、不派发 … 只写复核记录、认领行与门铃". Queue duty includes re-enqueueing flake victims, the front jump and, on main, the relay dequeue: all writes a review seat may not make. So with no queue seat open, two seats are told the duty is theirs and one of them is forbidden to do it. The card does say one review seat owned queue duty in the pilot, but queue.md was written after that and is the owner. Fix: make the line a pure pointer (queue duty follows lanes/queue.md, fallback included), or change queue.md and review.md under their own cards.
- **S2 (should-fix) — review seats opened by the lane meet the review charter's independence line.** area-lease.md lines 13 and 28 have the lane scale review seats and open one project thread per review seat, citing lanes/review.md. That charter says "⛔ 不复核本账号派发或实现的 PR". In the pilot the review seats were opened inside the lane's own project on the maintainer's word for the pilot (「你这里的复审也有你单独开座位」, #33059), which the general text does not carry. A lane following both files literally cannot use the seats it just opened. Second half of the same finding: line 44 routes every owed PR to "本区复核席", while contract-review.md says routing lives only there (self-review when the lane can take the tier, otherwise knock any seated review seat, idle one takes). Fix in one line: say whose account may sit an area's review seat, or say these threads are the lane's isolated at-tier reviewers under contract-review.md rather than `review#N` seats, and leave "who is knocked" to contract-review.md.
- **S3 (should-fix) — "协调线程 ⛔ 不读 diff、日志" is undefined and collides with the seat's own read.** Line 41. The file never says which threads are coordination threads. If area threads are included, the line forbids what contract-review.md requires for a PR that touches none of the four faces ("CI 加席位自读 ⛔ 不起第二个 agent") and what SKILL.md requires at ACCEPT (the seat corrects the six lines against the diff it read itself). Two ⛔ lines then point opposite ways on every ordinary PR an area lands. Fix: name the thread meant (the seat thread, per lesson 7), or state that the area's ACCEPT read is the exception.
- **S4 (should-fix) — the file does not say what an area thread is to the seat model.** Areas claim cards themselves (lines 38–40). seat-lifecycle.md reading three makes a seat stand down when the newest `Claim:` under its seat number comes from another session within a round. With eight area sessions claiming under one seat number, the seat thread and every area trip that reading on each other. The lease table has a "线程" column that could carry the answer, but no sentence connects it. Fix: one line saying area sessions listed in the lease table are the seat's own work for the opening mutual-exclusion readings, and which session and seat signature an area's `Claim:` carries.
- **N1 (nit)** — line 26 "试点或专题卡开始评论": "试点" is pilot residue; other lanes have no pilot card.
- **N2 (nit)** — line 53 "在座位贴记一行" does not say comment or body; seat-post-protocol.md keeps shift narrative out of the body. Read as a comment.
- **N3 (nit, follow-up card)** — the `lease:` label family has no row in `scripts/pm/ensure-pm-labels.sh`, while SKILL.md says a label exists only with a named reader and the vocabulary script's notes are the authority. The objects already exist in the repo (eight pilot labels) and label-write does not refuse them, so nothing breaks. Outside this diff: the seat files the card.
- **N4 (nit)** — line 50 "改可见行为或读 ADR … 呈维护者": "读 ADR" is everyday work; the card's word is "interprets". As a pointer to 升级与决策 the line is safe, since that section decides what escalates.
- **N5 (nit)** — line 34 points closing at SKILL.md 域车道; that section owns grading, while "do not close on your own reading" lives in execution-duties.md. The pointer is loose, not wrong.

No must-fix. S1 to S4 are each a one-line change in area-lease.md, which sits at headroom 0: pay by compressing in place (the worked example is the obvious place), not by a further raise. Their fix moves the head and earns a delta review from this reviewer; the PR is not landable on this record alone, because the landing pre-check requires a current-head PASS with no should-fix open.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-g5qfeh`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f2ea54651503723551da525b0694b514f829739`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md + scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs

Delta review from `b741f8255d645c9ab72053afb28cd4cd4d3c4a56` to this head, on top of record 6893242470. The two heads were diffed directly: one commit, one file, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md`, 15 lines in and 15 out. SKILL.md, seat-lifecycle.md and the ratchet script are byte-identical to the prior head, so ①, ② and ③ of the prior record stand and are not re-argued.

Inputs read: card #33751 body and both comments (claim 6892768967, dev report 6893055822); PR #33777 body (its Review fixes section included) and the delta; record 6893242470; the cited owners in the head tree and on main `b76df9a6980d` (lanes/queue.md, lanes/review.md, contract-review.md, seat-lifecycle.md, execution-duties.md, landing-operations.md, platform-readings.md, SKILL.md), and the claim readers on main (scripts/check-closing-target-claim.mjs, scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs, scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs), read and not reviewed.

Check-runs on this head: 48 runs, all completed, none pending at the last read: 26 success, 22 skipped, 0 failed. `Test Core (1/8)` was in progress at the first read and completed success, as did the `Test Core` aggregate. `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (the line ratchet among its gates), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both `PR-body guards` runs and both `Test Core` shards are success. One reading for the seat: both `Check Changeset` runs on this head are skipped, where the prior head had one success and one skipped; the PR carries `skip-changeset` and nothing published changes, so this is a landing-time reading for the seat and not a finding.

### ① Derived judgments

- Unchanged from the prior record: no accept set or public surface change, Tier S, authoring tier compensated by the at-tier read (this record continues it), both ordinary raises and the new ratchet rows right in amount and authority.
- Line budget on this head: area-lease.md is 60 lines, longest line 120 bytes, no table row; the ratchet rows (60, table row 0) are untouched and still equal the file. No ceiling row moved in the delta. The fixes were paid in place.
- Main moved under the PR (merge base `12a0f09fca49`; main since touched lanes/queue.md, landing-operations.md and the ratchet script). The owner lines this delta points at still hold on main: queue.md keeps its no-seat fallback line, contract-review.md keeps the routing line. The ratchet script will need its usual merge with main at landing; that is outside this delta.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset` matches the diff. Clause-②: no, confirmed from the committed tree.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Unchanged from the prior record for the three declared omissions, the trailer and the relay author.
- New in the delta: the card's "one review seat owns merge-queue duty" is now not written at all. Sound: lanes/queue.md is the owner and gives the fallback to triage, and lanes/review.md forbids a review seat the queue's writes. The PR body says so. The seat names it in its ACCEPT with the other accepted deviations from card section 3.
- New in the delta: the card's "start comment on the pilot/epic card" (section 2.3 item 1) is dropped whole, where N1 only named the word 试点. Nothing is lost: seat-lifecycle.md already has every seating post `seat-online` and a seating audit comment.
- Security: none found.

### ④ Design judgment

Prior findings on this head:

- S1 closed. Line 14 is a pure pointer: queue duty follows lanes/queue.md only, its no-seat fallback included, and the file assigns nothing itself. It agrees with queue.md in the head tree and on main.
- S2 closed. Line 13 puts review seats on another account and cites lanes/review.md; the same account may sit one only on the maintainer's own word. Line 25 opens one project thread per area only and sends review threads to that line. Line 44 leaves whether, whom, tier and head moves to contract-review.md and no longer names an area's review seat. This agrees with review.md (routing lives in contract-review.md, any seated review seat is knocked, the idle one takes; no review of the own account's work) and with contract-review.md's routing line. Two leftovers are nits N6 and N7 below.
- S3 closed. Line 40 sends writing and development-time reading through sub-agents; line 41 names the seat thread and excepts the ACCEPT self-read with both owners cited. Area threads keep the self-read contract-review.md and SKILL.md require on the PRs they land. One read is still caught by the letter, nit N8.
- S4 partly closed. The signature and `Session:` half is answered and passes the claim readers. The stand-down half is answered for one reading out of two and without a reader scope: S5 and S6 below.
- N1, N2, N4, N5 taken. N5's new line (closing follows execution-duties.md, never on the area's own reading) agrees with that file's own "do not close it yourself". N3 stays the seat's follow-up card.
- Worked example, six lines to four: nothing the card orders as a rule is lost. The card orders the split as a starting point to re-derive, and the lead still says starting point, re-derived each shift, other lanes derive their own. One blur, nit N9.

Claim shape (asked): passes. `check:closing-target-claim` reads `h46ClaimNamesBranch`: a first line `Claim:` after at most one signature line, and a `Branch:` naming the PR head branch; line 38 keeps `Branch:` on AGENTS.md naming. `post-stamped` and `label-write` refuse an unsigned body by shape only (lane, seat number, account, session id), and the claim's keyed lines need a readable `Seat:`, `Thread-read:`, `Clause-②:` and container line; none compares the signature's session with `Session:`. `claimSessionId` reads the claim's own session, so a yield by the area session still withdraws its own claim. An area claim signed with the seat's lane, number and account and carrying the area session in `Session:` is read as written.

New findings:

- **S5 (should-fix) — the exemption covers reading three only, and lives outside its owner.** Line 36 says claims by lease-table sessions do not count as reading three. seat-lifecycle.md reading four reads the newest closed lane card carrying a `Claim:` under the same seat number and takes its session id; at the pilot's rate that card is an area session's almost every round, so the seat still stands down on its own areas, by the reading next to the one exempted. The push limb of reading three ("a push is a claim") is not named either. And the pointer is one-way: seat-lifecycle.md is read at every fire before the first write, area-lease.md only at seating, hand-over and shift, and seat-lifecycle.md says the references are re-read after the exclusion clears. A fresh seat session after a rotation meets readings three and four with no exception in sight. seat-lifecycle.md already keeps its exemptions in one line that speaks of both readings ("评审链与总监席的笔迹是跨席作业不算占席;读数三、四只增加自退"). Fix at zero line cost: add the lease-table area sessions to that line in seat-lifecycle.md (the file is in this PR and stays at 100), and let line 36 point at it.
- **S6 (should-fix) — the exemption has no reader scope, so it removes the one trace that cannot be omitted.** Tried to break it. A session not on the lease table cannot exempt its own claims: the table is on the seat post, whose body only the incumbent edits, so its claims count as before. But the line is written for any reader. In this mode the seat thread claims nothing; the areas do. A second session arriving on the same seat number (a duplicate fire, a recovery after the usage wall, a new account while the old one drains) reads the table, discounts every area claim, and finds reading three empty. seat-lifecycle.md says the opening marker may be missed and the claim may not, so with the marker missed nothing claim-based stops the second seat session. Fix in the same sentence as S5: the claims do not count between the seat post's current PM session and the sessions on its table; to a session that is neither, they count as they do today.

Stale lease row (asked): judged safe. The exemption does not touch a card's own claim; line 37 still keeps every other session off a claimed card, and release and reclaim are unchanged, so a stale row cannot keep a dead area's claims alive on a card. Its only effect is that the seat does not stand down against a session the table still names, and the table is rewritten when any column changes and re-decided at every hand-over. The failure runs the safe way round: an area thread that rotated and is not yet re-listed trips the seat. See N10.

- **N6 (nit)** — line 13's same-account exception is written here only; lanes/review.md still carries the unconditional line, so a review session reading its charter alone refuses. "本线程" also does not say which thread; read as the review thread.
- **N7 (nit)** — the lease table keeps a 复核席 column (line 12, as the card orders) while line 44 now routes by contract-review.md alone. The column is a record with no reader.
- **N8 (nit)** — line 41 still catches one read by its letter: a red check on a PR the seat lands, where platform-readings.md says read the log first and landing-operations.md's three facts need the failing file against the diff. Neither rule says the seat thread must read it in its own context, so a sub-agent satisfies both; the line does not say so.
- **N9 (nit)** — the compressed example dropped A5's "action routes excepted", so A5 runtime and E2b runtime action routes now overlap on their face, in a file whose line 10 asks that two areas rarely touch the same function.
- **N10 (nit)** — line 36 speaks of sessions on the lease table, but the table's column is 线程. A rotation at about 150k changes the session and arguably not the thread, so no rewrite is triggered. Say the column carries the thread's session id.
- **N11 (nit)** — "署本席签名" does not say which session fills the signature's third slot. Both readings pass the shape recogniser; the precedent on this card (dev report 6893055822) is the writing session.

No must-fix. S5 and S6 are one sentence in seat-lifecycle.md plus a pointer in area-lease.md line 36; neither needs a new line or a ceiling move. The fix moves the head and earns a delta review from this reviewer. The PR is not landable on this record alone, because the landing pre-check requires a current-head PASS with no should-fix open.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0d547f0d9a3ba2b2c21de356f68ce09a9ea524a5`
Local-runs: probe — the requesting seat asked for the skill gates and the merge to be re-measured on this head; listed under ① and run in a detached worktree
Scope: .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/area-lease.md, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-lifecycle.md + scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs

DELTA review from `8f2ea54651503723551da525b0694b514f829739` (record 6893494266: PASS, should-fix S5 and S6, nits N6 to N11) to this head, taken on handoff 6893693514 and claim 6893740967. First record: 6893242470. The earlier records were rendered by an isolated reviewer adopted by the lane seat; this delta is rendered by the review seat, on another account than the one that dispatched and implemented the PR.

Inputs read: card 33751 body and both comments (claim 6892768967, dev report 6893055822); PR 33777 body with its round 2 section, its four files and all four comments; both prior records in full; the head tree of seat-lifecycle.md, area-lease.md, seat-post-protocol.md, lanes/review.md, lanes/queue.md, landing-operations.md, execution-duties.md and contract-review.md, the owners read and not reviewed.

Shape of the move, measured: the head is `8f2ea546` plus two commits. `4106cebe` merges main at `1e65a389`; `git merge-tree --write-tree` of its two parents returns tree `24e75a54`, identical to the merge commit's tree, so the merge is clean and carries no hand resolution. `0d547f0d` is the one authored commit: two files, 4 lines in and 4 out. PR against main: 4 files, 89 in and 3 out.

Check-runs on this head: 48, all completed, 26 success, 22 skipped, none red, none pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, public surface, governed tier and semver reading are unchanged from the prior records: three `.claude/**` rule files and one PM gate script, Tier S.
- Zero net lines holds: SKILL.md 320, seat-lifecycle.md 100, area-lease.md 60, each equal to its ceiling row; the longest area-lease.md line is 120 bytes.
- No ceiling row moved in the delta. The ratchet script's hunks against main are byte-identical to its hunks at `8f2ea546` against the old merge base: the same two ordinary raises, the one new ceiling row and the one new table-row pin.
